title: Complete characterization of internal-external entanglement trade-offs in two-mode Gaussian states
abstract: We characterize the exact trade-off between internal and external entanglement in asymmetric two-mode Gaussian states at fixed local symplectic eigenvalues. Internal entanglement is quantified by the negativity $\mathcal{N}_{A:B}$ between the two modes, while external entanglement is quantified by the negativity $\mathcal{N}_{AB:CD}$ across a Gaussian purification. Numerical sampling suggests the boundary structure of the attainable region in the $(\mathcal{N}_{AB:CD},\mathcal{N}_{A:B})$ plane, which we then determine analytically. Parametrizing the global symplectic spectrum yields a closed admissible interval for the remaining spectral parameter at fixed $\mathcal{N}_{AB:CD}$. We prove constructively that every point in this interval corresponds to a physical covariance matrix, implying that all intermediate values of $\mathcal{N}_{A:B}$ between the resulting sharp bounds are achievable. The upper bound is attained for opposite-sign correlations of equal magnitude, while the positive branch of the lower bound occurs when one global symplectic eigenvalue equals unity. We also identify two external-entanglement thresholds, derive a saturated monogamy-type inequality, and recover the symmetric-state limit.
summary: This paper rigorously characterizes the complete trade-off boundary between internal and external entanglement for two-mode Gaussian states. By combining numerical evidence with deep analytical techniques involving symplectic spectra, the authors derive sharp, achievable bounds for the entanglement measures. This work establishes a fundamental monogamy-type inequality governing entanglement resource allocation in these quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to characterize the exact trade-off relationship between internal entanglement and external entanglement for two-mode Gaussian states.
main_result: The authors derive the complete, piecewise-defined, and physically achievable region in the entanglement plane, establishing sharp bounds and a saturated monogamy-type inequality.
method: The analysis combines numerical sampling to suggest bounds with rigorous analytical techniques involving parameterizing the global symplectic spectrum and deriving necessary spectral constraints.
model_or_system: The study focuses on asymmetric two-mode Gaussian states, which are mathematically characterized using covariance matrices and their associated symplectic eigenvalues.
key_observables: Internal entanglement (Negativity $\mathcal{N}_{A:B}$) and external entanglement (Negativity $\mathcal{N}_{AB:CD}$) are the primary observables.
important_parameters: Local symplectic eigenvalues ($a, b$), global symplectic spectrum parameters ($C, z$), and entanglement thresholds ($\alpha, \beta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the state is a two-mode Gaussian state and relies on establishing necessary spectral constraints to prove the sufficiency of the derived bounds.
figures_summary: Figure 2 numerically plots the relationship between $\mathcal{N}_{A:B}$ and $\mathcal{N}_{AB:CD}$ for various state parameters, overlaid with the analytically derived upper and lower bounding curves ($g_2$ and $g_1$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the problem and using numerical evidence to derive necessary spectral constraints, then analytically determining the admissible parameter ranges, and finally proving the sharpness of the bounds via constructive reconstruction and deriving a monogamy-type inequality.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental, rigorous constraints on entanglement measures for Gaussian states, which are crucial building blocks in quantum optics and quantum information theory, directly impacting resource quantification.

Green denotes physical PPT (separable) states, red denotes physical NPT (entangled) states, and pale gray denotes unphysical covariance matrices. The outer boundary is set by physicality, while the internal boundary is given by eν−= 1. The axes have the same range in all panels.

FIG. 2. Internal negativity NA:B versus external negativity NAB:CD for a = 2 and b = 1.01, 1.5, 2, 2.5. Blue points are physical standard-form states drawn from 290 000 uniformly sampled pairs (c1, c2) per panel before physicality selection; the respective numbers of retained points are 3733, 114998, 156064, and 171204. Red and green curves show the proposed upper and positive lower envelopes g2 and g1, whose exactness and attainability are established analytically below. The dotted and dashed vertical lines mark α and β, respectively.
